title: The 25 Best Center Backs in World Soccer—Ranked
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By SI FC StaffJul 9, 2025Gabriel (left) and William Saliba lead the way for Arsenal. / Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesFinding a truly elite center back in today’s game is like striking gold. It’s one of the most demanding positions on the pitch—requiring not just physical dominance and razor-sharp instincts, but also the leadership to marshal an entire back line and the composure to thrive under pressure.
Just to compete, central defenders also need the ability to be able to play out from the back, demonstrating a coolness in possession like you’ve never seen before.
Over the years, only a select few have truly mastered the art—and even fewer are still performing at the highest level today. That makes narrowing down a definitive top 25 no easy task.
After extensive debate, Sports Illustrated has attempted to narrow down those who cover all possible skillsets to the highest level—with the rankings fluctuating and changing all the time.

Romero is now an Atletico player. / Nicolò Campo/LightRocket/Getty ImagesChristian Romero is a defender carved from granite and pure adrenaline. He flies into tackles like they’re personal battles, attacks headers like a missile and plays with an intensity that feels borrowed from another era. Few defenders fight harder. Few care more.And he knows how to win. A World Cup champion, two-time Copa América winner and Europa League winner with Tottenham, Romero has a knack for rising to the occasion. There’s every chance more silverware follows at Atlético Madrid.But his greatest strength is also his biggest weakness. That raw, emotional, all-or-nothing style can tip into chaos—reckless challenges, needless bookings and moments of madness that can change a game.Romero has everything you want in a defender, except, sometimes, the brakes.

Jan Paul van Hecke is going from strength to strength.  / Vince Mignott/MB Media/Getty ImagesIf you want to define the modern day, ball-playing center back, Jan Paul van Hecke might be the name on the tip of your tongue.The Dutchman is supremely composed in defense, hence why Tottenham Hotspur forked out over £50 million to sign him from Brighton & Hove Albion in the summer of 2026, but its what he can do to spring danger in the other direction that has got everybody talking.Van Hecke has a tremendous range of passing and is more than happy to walk the ball out of defense and into midfield himself. He’s two-footed, strong and has quick thinking—attributes that are needed to play for a club with Spurs’ aspirations, as well as being a starter in the Netherlands national team.

A summer move to Arsenal rewarded Hincapie’s progress. / David Ramos/Getty ImagesSouth American defenders have long been associated with aggression, and Ecuadorian center back Piero Hincapié fits that mold perfectly.Always on the front foot and willing to push high to press, Hincapié can occasionally overstep the mark, but the payoff far outweighs the risk. His tenacity disrupts opponents, wins the ball in dangerous areas and sparks transitions, while his sharp positioning and crisp distribution allow him to move possession forward quickly.That approach thrived under Xabi Alonso at Bayer Leverkusen, where Hincapié played a key role in their historic unbeaten Bundesliga title run in 2023–24 before carrying that winning habit to Arsenal’s 2025–26 Premier League triumph.Wherever Hincapié goes, success seems to follow.

Micky van de Ven has admirers at Liverpool. / James Gill/Danehouse/Getty ImagesThe only thing holding Micky van de Ven back from climbing higher on this list? Injuries. They robbed him of rhythm during his debut season at Tottenham in 2023–24 and derailed the campaign that followed. But when fit, Van de Ven is an absolute nightmare for attackers.Why? He’s officially the Premier League’s fastest player since speed tracking began in 2021, and few forwards can live with him in a footrace. His absurd pace leaves attackers with two choices: try to dribble past those freakishly long legs—or simply go around him. Spoiler: most smart strikers choose the latter.When Van de Ven is fit and flying, he’s almost impossible to beat. And if he can finally stay healthy, his ceiling is frighteningly high.

Antonio Rüdiger is no longer a reliable option for Real Madrid. / Guillermo Martinez/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesAntonio Rüdiger is—if there’s a better way to put it—a character. Whether he’s charging up the pitch with his knees pumping like pistons and tongue hanging out in celebration, or simply causing chaos, he’s one of soccer’s most entertaining sights. Bonkers? A little. Unmissable? Absolutely.That same wild energy fuels him on the field. He’s a fearless competitor, throwing himself into tackles and chasing attackers with an intensity few can match.But don’t mistake the chaos for a lack of control. Rüdiger has a sharp soccer brain, reads the game brilliantly and is rarely caught out of position. He’s also comfortable on the ball, even if his infamous Chelsea screamer against Brentford occasionally tempts him into trying the spectacular a little too often.In an era of system-perfect defenders, Rüdiger is the glorious exception—a maverick who defends with instinct, intensity and sheer presence.

Akanji a smart both on and off the pitch. / DeFodi Images/Getty ImagesManuel Akanji is famously sharp off the pitch—so much so that he’s known for solving complex mathematical problems in seconds. But that brainpower doesn’t stay in the classroom—it’s all over his game.He plays soccer with the same level of intelligence: calculated, composed, and always seemingly one move ahead.Versatile in both position and style, the Swiss international can adapt to almost any challenge thrown his way. Whether operating as a center back or filling in across the back line, Akanji handles situations with a calm precision that makes defending look effortless.Striker drifting to the edge of the box? That’s not a problem—it’s a move Akanji saw coming three passes ago. Like a chess grandmaster, he’s already mapped out the board and shut down the angle before the opponent even realises it was an option.

Éder Militão has been plagued by injury. / Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesWhen Éder Militão was presented as a Real Madrid player upon his arrival in 2019, he was so overwhelmed by the occasion that he had to cut his introductory press conference short to avoid fainting.That timidity has been emphatically washed away over the subsequent years.Accomplished with the ball at his feet and a supreme reader of the game ahead of him, Militão is the complete defensive package. Yet, even Achilles had a dodgy heel. The Brazil international has been beset by fitness issues in recent years, keeping him from the pitch and any higher up this list.

Dias is still top class. / Neal Simpson/Sportsphoto/Allstar/Getty ImagesRúben Dias may no longer be the all-conquering defensive force who swept the FWA Footballer of the Year and Premier League Player of the Season awards in 2020–21, but he remains one of the world’s finest center backs.The Portuguese was a cornerstone of Manchester City’s historic 2022–23 treble and played a major role again as they retained the Premier League title the following season. Vocal, fiercely competitive and rarely afraid to demand more from those around him, Dias has often been City’s on-field leader in a team overflowing with talent but sometimes short on natural voices of authority.Lately, mistakes have crept into his game and his confidence has occasionally appeared fragile. But that dip feels more connected to City’s broader struggles than any dramatic decline in Dias himself.

Real Madrid are chasing Nico Schlotterbeck. / Ralf Ibing/firo sportphoto/Getty ImagesNico Schlotterbeck cuts a relatively unassuming figure, but don’t let that fool you. The Borussia Dortmund star has quietly developed into one of Germany’s most complete and exciting center backs.A key figure for Dortmund, Schlotterbeck offers far more than defensive solidity. He’s an aggressive, front-foot defender who isn’t afraid to step out, win challenges and carry the ball into midfield. That progressive streak, paired with his composure under pressure, makes him a hugely valuable weapon when building from the back.No longer simply a promising talent, Schlotterbeck has grown into a genuine leader—and one of the finest defenders in Germany.

Luka Vušković is ready to make his name in the Premier League. / Steve Bardens/Getty ImagesTo call Luka Vušković’s loan spell at Hamburg successful would be a serious understatement. The swashbuckling defender was so impressive that fans voted him the Bundesliga’s best player of the 2025–26 season midway through the campaign, despite playing for a side simply aiming for mid-table safety.A towering presence at both ends of the pitch, Vušković made such an impression that Hamburg openly pleaded with Tottenham to extend his loan for another season. Instead, Spurs sold him to Brighton—a puzzling decision given their own desperate need for defensive reinforcements.

Konate joined Real Madrid in the summer. / Diego Souto/Getty ImagesSometimes calling a big center back a “physical beast” feels lazy. In Ibrahima Konaté’s case, though, it’s simply accurate. The Real Madrid defender is a human wall—towering, powerful and capable of bullying almost anyone who comes his way.Just look at the 2022 FA Cup final, when a young Konaté was tasked with dealing with Romelu Lukaku, one of the most physically imposing strikers in the game. He barely gave the Belgian a sniff, dominating the aerial battles, tackles and physical duels throughout.Since then, Konaté has added considerably more to his game. His immense strength is now complemented by better positioning, greater composure and a sharper reading of the game, giving him a more complete defensive skill set without sacrificing his aggression.Mistakes have started to creep into his game, but when Konaté is at his best, few center backs in the world are more difficult to beat.

Chelsea snapped up Lacroix in the summer. / Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty ImagesMaxence Lacroix’s rise has been quite remarkable.In just six seasons, he has gone from a Ligue 2 struggler with Sochaux to a Bundesliga regular with VfL Wolfsburg, a cup and European trophy winner with Crystal Palace, and now a key figure at the heart of Chelsea’s defense.He’s also established himself as a regular for France, playing a prominent role at the 2026 World Cup.Strong and tall but remarkably athletic, Lacroix combines his physical gifts with composure on the ball and a willingness to drive forward and contribute in attack.It’s quite the journey—and he’s clearly not finished climbing yet.

Gleison Bremer's importance to Juventus is highlighted by key statistics. / IMAGO/BuzziLike Micky van de Ven, Gleison Bremer is another elite center back whose momentum has been stalled by injury—missing most of the 2024–25 campaign with an ACL tear.One of the biggest compliments you can pay him? Juventus noticed. Without Bremer’s physical dominance and technical quality at the heart of their defense, the Old Lady looked lost. With him in the lineup for the first six Serie A matches, they kept six clean sheets.After his injury? Just 11 shutouts in the remaining 31 games—not a disaster, but a clear drop-off, and a testament to just how important Bremer is, not only for his own defending but for organizing the entire back line. When he's healthy, he elevates everything—and everyone—around him.

Joško Gvardiol has only improved since joining Manchester City. / IMAGO/SportimageAs is often the case with Pep Guardiola’s signings, Joško Gvardiol needed some time to settle at Manchester City. The Croatia international spent much of his first season at the Etihad at left back before gradually moving into the center, where he eventually established himself as a regular during the 2025–26 campaign.“I'm happy to be back to my position,” Gvardiol beamed before summing up his style with the type of efficiency which is a defining factor of his game: “Just play simple, protect the goal, defend the goal.”

Jonathan Tah’s credentials were proven at Bayer Leverkusen. /  Lars Baron/Getty ImagesBayern Munich have long made a habit of raiding the Bundesliga for its brightest stars, and Jonathan Tah is the latest jewel they’ve added to the crown.Tah was a pillar of Bayer Leverkusen’s historic 2023–24 unbeaten domestic campaign, helping the club secure its first-ever Bundesliga title. He was just as dependable the following season, even as Leverkusen fell short of repeating the feat.Eventually, though, the move happened. Bayern got their man.A popular transfer in the eyes of Leverkusen fans? Not likely. But it says a lot about Tah: cool-headed, committed, relentlessly professional. He gave everything before the switch—no drama, no ego, just performances that screamed elite.And since arriving in Bavaria? Back-to-back Bundesliga titles have made the transfer look every bit as shrewd as Bayern hoped.
